lines.text: But dearest—Did you not understand that I understood?
lines.note: Elizabeth opens with the intimate assurance that she already understands him.

lines.text: How I wish for two hearts to love you with, and two lives to give to you, and two souls to bear the weight worthily of all you have given to me.
lines.note: Elizabeth wishes for two hearts and lives to give to Robert.

lines.text: Well,—I am yours, you are mine, dearest Ba!
lines.note: Robert answers that they belong wholly to each other.

lines.text: I have lost my poor Flush—lost him!
lines.note: Elizabeth's anguished report that Flush has been stolen.

lines.text: Was ever any in the world, in any possible world, so perfectly good and dear to another as you are to me!
lines.note: Elizabeth marvels at Robert's goodness and dearness.

lines.text: To be parted from you so long, teaches me the necessity of your presence—I am your very, very own.
lines.note: Elizabeth says separation teaches the necessity of his presence.

lines.text: Only a few words to tell you that Flush is found, and lying on the sofa, with one paw and both ears hanging over the edge of it.
lines.note: Elizabeth announces Flush is found after the theft.

lines.text: Also I will ever say, God bless you, my dearest dearest,—my perfect angel you have been!
lines.note: Robert calls Elizabeth his perfect angel.

lines.text: Dearest, I write one word, and have one will which is yours.
lines.note: Elizabeth gives one will that is entirely his.

lines.text: Words can never tell you, however,—form them, transform them anyway,—how perfectly dear you are to me—perfectly dear to my heart and soul.
lines.note: Robert says words cannot tell how perfectly dear she is.

lines.text: And forgive the inveterate jesting, which jests with eyes full of tears.
lines.note: Elizabeth's jesting is made with eyes full of tears.

lines.text: By to-morrow at this time, I shall have you only, to love me—my beloved!
lines.note: Elizabeth looks forward to having only Robert to love her.
